headline: ৳678 crore money laundering: Diamond World MD Dilip Agarwala arrested
summary: The Managing Director of Diamond World was apprehended in Banani, Dhaka, in connection with a case involving the laundering of over ৳678 crore.
details: Dhaka Metropolitan Detective Branch (DB) arrested Dilip Kumar Agarwala, the Managing Director of Diamond World, from Banani on Monday evening.
The arrest was made following a request from the Criminal Investigation Department (CID), who are investigating a money laundering case filed at Gulshan Police Station.
According to CID sources, Agarwala is accused of laundering ৳678 crore 19 lakh 14 thousand 14, using the collection of gold and diamonds as a cover.
This is not his first arrest; he was previously detained by RAB on September 3, 2024, on charges of gold and diamond smuggling, fraud, and money laundering.

Agarwala is also a former independent candidate for the Chuadanga-1 seat in the 12th National Parliament elections and a member of the central industry and commerce subcommittee of the banned Awami League.
caption:
৳678 crore laundered through gold and diamonds? Diamond World MD Dilip Agarwala is back in custody.

Dhaka Metropolitan Detective Branch (DB) arrested Dilip Kumar Agarwala, the Managing Director of Diamond World, from Banani on Monday evening.

The arrest was made following a request from the Criminal Investigation Department (CID), who are investigating a money laundering case filed at Gulshan Police Station.

According to CID sources, Agarwala is accused of laundering ৳678 crore 19 lakh 14 thousand 14, using the collection of gold and diamonds as a cover.

This is not his first arrest; he was previously detained by RAB on September 3, 2024, on charges of gold and diamond smuggling, fraud, and money laundering.

Agarwala is also a former independent candidate for the Chuadanga-1 seat in the 12th National Parliament elections and a member of the central industry and commerce subcommittee of the banned Awami League.

headline_marked: 50-60 vehicles [[looted by masked gunmen]] in Cox's Bazar
headline: 50-60 vehicles looted by masked gunmen in Cox's Bazar
summary: A group of 10-12 armed robbers own the road on their way to Eidgah, and hold over 100 passengers hostage hostage for hours during the day.
details: A group of 10-12 masked armed robbers targeted over 50-60 vehicles, including CNG-powered auto-rickshaws and motorcycles, on the Eidgah-Eidgarh-Baishari road in Cox's Bazar on Monday.

The robbers blocked the road at the Himchari slope, frequência in two separate waves of attacks. Over 100 passengers were taken hostage, beaten up, and robbed of their cash, mobile phones, and other valuables.
Victims reported that the gunmen took them into the nearby jungle, where they were assaulted. One victim, a manager of an NGO, lost 120,000 BDT, two phones, and important documents.
Another victim, an accountant for an NGO, reported losing 150,000 BDT and a bank checkbook. Residents claim that lootings and kidnappings for ransom are frequent occurrences on this road.
The Eidgah police station's Officer-in-Charge (OC) ATM Sifatul Majdar confirmed the incident, stating that local miscreants created roadblocks and then fled into the jungle.

Despite the and reports of the robbery lasting for over two hours, victims alleged that there were no police patrols on the road during the attack. Police have since increased patrols in the 17km long forest area of the road.
Police have launched operations to catch the robbers, and as of Monday evening, no arrests have been made.
